title: Levels of Organization and Body Systems
seo_title: Levels of Organization Worksheets: Cells, Tissues, Organs and Systems (Biology)
standard_text: Develop and use a model to illustrate the hierarchical organization of interacting systems that provide specific functions within multicellular organisms.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on levels of organization (NGSS HS-LS1-2): cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and how systems work together. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Organ systems work together to keep the whole organism alive.
body_html:
How to think about it

Small parts build bigger parts. Many cells form a tissue; tissues form an organ; organs form a system; systems form an organism.

  • Each system has a job (circulatory, respiratory, digestive, nervous...).
  • Systems work together: lungs load oxygen, the heart moves it, muscles use it.
Example

Cardiac muscle: which level?

Many similar cells, one job

Answer: tissue

Example

You run. Which systems speed up together?

Muscles need more oxygen

Lungs and heart supply it

Answer: respiratory and circulatory

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a tissue is bigger than an organ.
  • Putting the heart in the respiratory system.
  • Thinking each system works alone.

faq.q: What are the levels of organization?
faq.a: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism, from smallest to largest.

faq.q: How do body systems work together?
faq.a: During exercise, the respiratory system takes in oxygen, the circulatory system delivers it and the nervous system speeds both up.
Yes. The root system takes in water and minerals, and the shoot system (stems, leaves, flowers) makes food and reproduces.

items.q: What does the nervous system do?
c: sends signals to control and coordinate the body
items.e: Brain, spinal cord, nerves.

items.q: What is the main job of the respiratory system?
c: take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide
items.e: Lungs exchange gases.

items.q: Which level of organization is a root hair cell?
items.e: A root hair cell is a cell.

items.q: Where do oxygen and carbon dioxide move between the lungs and blood?
items.e: Tiny air sacs with capillaries.

items.q: Which level of organization is an oak tree?
items.e: An oak tree is an organism.

items.q: What is the main job of the circulatory system?
c: carry blood with oxygen and nutrients around the body
items.e: Heart and blood vessels.

items.q: Which level is the largest?
items.e: An organism is made of all its systems.

items.q: Which level of organization is the shoot system of a plant?
items.e: The shoot system of a plant is an organ system.

items.q: Which level of organization is a muscle cell?
items.e: A muscle cell is a cell.

items.q: Which level of organization is a human?
items.e: A human is an organism.

items.q: What is an organ?
c: a structure made of different tissues working together
items.e: The heart has muscle, nerve and connective tissue.

items.q: Which level of organization is a lung?
items.e: A lung is an organ.

items.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
c: cell → tissue → organ system → organ → organism
tissue → cell → organ → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
cell → organ → tissue → organ system → organism
items.e: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems.

items.q: Which level of organization is the circulatory system?
items.e: The circulatory system is an organ system.

items.q: Which is the smallest level of organization in an organism?
items.e: The cell is the basic unit of life.

items.q: Which level of organization is a neuron?
items.e: A neuron is a cell.

items.q: What is the job of the excretory system?
items.e: Kidneys filter blood.

items.q: What level is made of many cells working together?
items.e: Many cells make up a tissue.

items.q: What is a tissue?
c: a group of similar cells doing the same job
items.e: Cells → tissue.

items.q: Which level of organization is a skin cell?
items.e: A skin cell is a cell.

items.q: Which organ system does the trachea belong to?
items.e: The trachea is part of the respiratory system.

items.q: What level comes right after tissue (going from small to large)?
items.e: tissue → organ.

items.q: Which level of organization is bone tissue?
items.e: Bone tissue is a tissue.

items.q: Which level of organization is a red blood cell?
items.e: A red blood cell is a cell.

items.q: Which organ system does the diaphragm belong to?
items.e: The diaphragm is part of the respiratory system.

items.q: Which organ system does the white blood cells belong to?
items.e: The white blood cells is part of the immune system.

items.q: Which organ system does the small intestine belong to?
items.e: The small intestine is part of the digestive system.

items.q: Which level of organization is a leaf?
items.e: A leaf is an organ.

items.q: Which level of organization is cardiac muscle?
items.e: Cardiac muscle is a tissue.

items.q: What level is made of many tissues working together?
items.e: Many tissues make up an organ.

items.q: Which level of organization is the lining of the stomach?
items.e: The lining of the stomach is a tissue.

items.q: Which level of organization is xylem?
items.e: Xylem is a tissue.

items.q: Which level of organization is the brain?
items.e: The brain is an organ.

items.q: Which organ system does the stomach belong to?
items.e: The stomach is part of the digestive system.

items.q: What level comes right after organ (going from small to large)?
items.e: organ → organ system.

items.q: What level comes right after organ system (going from small to large)?
items.e: organ system → organism.

items.q: Which level of organization is the stomach?
items.e: The stomach is an organ.

items.q: Which organ system does the kidneys belong to?
items.e: The kidneys is part of the excretory (urinary) system.

items.q: Which organ system does the bladder belong to?
items.e: The bladder is part of the excretory (urinary) system.

items.q: Which organ system does the pancreas (making insulin) belong to?
items.e: The pancreas (making insulin) is part of the endocrine system.

items.q: Lily runs hard for 10 minutes. What happens to the breathing rate?
items.e: It goes up to take in more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for removing wastes from the blood?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which organ system does the heart belong to?
items.e: The heart is part of the circulatory system.

items.q: Jack runs hard for 10 minutes. What happens to sweating?
items.e: It goes up to cool the body.

items.q: During Ravi's run, the heart rate goes up. Why?
c: to pump more oxygen-rich blood to the muscles
so more blood can go to working muscles
to take in more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide
items.e: The systems respond together.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for moving nutrients from food to cells?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for getting oxygen to muscle cells?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which organ system does the biceps belong to?
items.e: The biceps is part of the muscular system.

items.q: Which organ system does the spinal cord belong to?
items.e: The spinal cord is part of the nervous system.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for breathing faster when you run?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for standing up and walking?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

to take in more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide

items.e: It goes down so more blood can go to working muscles.

items.e: The skin is part of the integumentary system.

items.q: Zoe runs hard for 10 minutes. What happens to the amount of sugar the muscles use?
items.e: It goes up to release more energy in cellular respiration.

items.q: Which organ system does the femur belong to?
items.e: The femur is part of the skeletal system.

items.q: During Ruby's run, blood flow to the digestive system goes down. Why?
c: so more blood can go to working muscles
to pump more oxygen-rich blood to the muscles
to release more energy in cellular respiration
items.e: The systems respond together.

items.q: Which organ system does the blood vessels belong to?
items.e: The blood vessels is part of the circulatory system.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for pulling your hand away from a hot stove?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.
